title: Partial Sequential Composition
statement: For any two finite Turing machines $M_1,M_2$ over the Boolean alphabet, there is a finite Boolean Turing machine $M$ such that, for all Boolean words $x,w$, $M$ halts on input $x$ with output $w$ after some finite number of steps if and only if there is a Boolean word $y$ for which $M_1$ halts on input $x$ with output $y$ after some finite number of steps and $M_2$ halts on input $y$ with output $w$ after some finite number of steps.
hypotheses_covered: Two finite Turing machines $M_1,M_2$ over the Boolean alphabet
replaced:
For any two multi-tape Turing machines $M_1$ and $M_2$ over the Boolean
alphabet — with no totality or time hypotheses — there exists a machine $M$
such that for all Boolean words $x$ and $w$: $M$ halts on input $x$ with
output $w$ (within some number of steps) if and only if there is a Boolean
word $y$ such that $M_1$ halts on input $x$ with output $y$ and $M_2$ halts on
input $y$ with output $w$.  In particular, if $M_1$ diverges on $x$, or halts
but $M_2$ diverges on its output, then $M$ diverges on $x$.
